_readme: THE MERRIMACK AT EVERY GRAIN THE PUBLIC RECORD HOLDS (2026-10-17): the shipped scene plus five raster
sources dropped onto the one tree by file, no C++ per dataset (HIERARCHY 4.20: a source paints its own
level, the tree folds the rest). Coarse to fine, the ladder this scene exercises:
450 m   ETOPO 15 arc-second (inherited)      10 m  CUDEM 1/9 arc-second (data.bathy, the solver's grid)
1.5 m   noaa.inlethq: BlueTopo 4 m + USACE eHydro Newburyport Harbor channel surveys of 2025-09-08 (CS)
and 2025-10-07 (XC), cell means at 1.5 m, NAVD88 (harvest hqbathy; the eHydro index holds no
newer survey on 2026-10-17). Geographic NAD83, no vertical GeoKey: unit and datum declared here.
1 m     usace.ncmp2018: the 2018 USACE NCMP CZMIL topobathy lidar, bare earth, 25 of its 1 km tiles
around the mouth (19TCH 50-53 E, 38-46 N), UTM 19N, NAVD88 by GeoKey 5703; nodata where the
laser saw no bottom, so the HQ bed shows through the channel. Its `feather` (10 m) fades its
weight from every nodata edge and from the tiles the folder lacks, as from its box: before it,
the bare earth stood as a wall over the survey beneath at the water's edge (2026-10-17).
0.5 m   (OUT since Mark's review of 2026-10-17 evening) noaa.iocm2011.mllw, NOAA's IOCM orthomosaic of
2011-06-19 flown at LOW water: nine 2.5 km RGB tiles at D:/DataCache/GAGAME/iocm/2011_mllw_rgb
(NCEI 0103944, CC0). Under today's water it painted the photographed WATER -- the 2011 channel
black, the 2011 bars sand -- as the bed's colour, with the photo's hard edges. It comes back
behind a gate that weighs an ortho's pixel by whether the ground was above the water when it
was flown (its capture level against the height tree); until then the water read its own photo.
0.15 m  massgis.coq2023: a scene's `sources` REPLACE the base's (they do not merge by name), so the
shipped three -- the MassGIS orthos, the highlights overlay, the ETOPO 15-second ring -- are
repeated here. The first cut of this scene forgot them (found by Mark's eye, 2026-10-17 evening).
0.05 m  usgs.tnb2025.ortho: the nearest PUBLIC drone orthomosaic to the Merrimack -- USGS Woods Hole UAS
flight of 2025-06-02 at Town Neck Beach, Sandwich MA (Cape Cod Bay, 120 km south), 5 cm SfM,
UTM 19N; the RGBA copy makes the flight's white border transparent (alpha is fiber).
No public drone ortho of the Merrimack exists on 2026-10-17: USGS's PIEPR flights (2017-2019,
Plum Island marsh 5 km south of the mouth) released raw photos and GCPs only. See docs/
CONTENT_SCALING_2026-10-17.md for what was searched.
0.25 m  usgs.tnb2025.dsm: the same flight's lidar surface model, NAVD88 declared (no vertical GeoKey).
buildings: the OSM + Overture solids of scenes/demos/newburyport_buildings.json, the same lines.
Stack order is StackOrder's default (the coarser grain under the finer) except that noaa.inlethq is given
`over` 1: the 2025 survey stands over the 2018 lidar where both have a bottom, the lidar keeps the beach and
the bars the survey never saw. Both carry a `feather` of 10 m, so where either one's data ends inside the
other's the stack ramps over 10 m instead of stepping (RasterFileSource: the edge of the data, 2026-10-17).
Fixed time.start so that A/B stills against scenes/merrimack.json (run with the same --set time.start)
compare one instant. Views: the shipped `sea` (jetty tip), `mouth` and `bar` over the inlet, `tnb_high`
and `tnb_low` over the drone flight.

sources.name: noaa.inlethq
sources._over: the hydrographic survey stands OVER the 2018 lidar where both have a bottom: in the turbid channel a laser return can be the water's surface, a 2025 sounding is the better witness; the lidar keeps the beach and the bars the survey never saw. The survey itself stood +3 m too high until 2026-10-17 evening (eHydro depths taken as heights). Its `feather` fades its weight from every nodata edge (the land BlueTopo never covered) as from its box.
